description: CodeGenesis is a team of curious builders, developers & space enthusiasts passionate about AI/ML, software, data visualization and astronomy. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we're exploring Planet X & SPHEREx through an interactive astronomical data experience. We welcome contributors interested in Astronomy, AI/ML, Web Dev, Data Science, Scientific Data, UI/UX & Storytelling.
summary:
SPHEREx TimeLens is an interactive astronomical analysis platform developed by Team CodeGenesis for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms genuine SPHEREx infrared observations into an accessible time-domain observatory, enabling users to explore how celestial objects change across multiple epochs.

The platform integrates NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) Level-2 FITS data with scientific image processing, astrometric motion tracking, difference imaging, spectral analysis, and infrared light-curve visualization. Users can investigate stellar variability, identify moving-object candidates, examine spectral signatures, and explore potential trans-Neptunian objects relevant to the Planet X search.

What makes SPHEREx TimeLens distinctive is its foundation in Karl Popper's Scientific Falsification Principle. Rather than presenting every unusual observation as a discovery, it tests hypotheses against measurable statistical thresholds, uncertainties, and null hypotheses. Its verification framework distinguishes supported candidates, rejected hypotheses, non-detections, and inconclusive results.

Our goal is to make advanced astronomical investigation transparent, reproducible, and accessible while helping users understand what the evidence actually supports.
details:
SPHEREx TimeLens — Technical Implementation and Project Impact

1. What Does the Project Do?

SPHEREx TimeLens is an interactive, web-based infrared astronomical observatory designed to explore how celestial objects change over time using observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission. It allows users to enter Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates, explore available observation epochs, compare infrared images, track potential moving objects, analyze spectral signatures, and investigate time-variable astronomical phenomena.

The platform aims to make complex astronomical observations accessible to students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts while providing scientific tools for investigating potential trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs), infrared transients, and objects relevant to the Planet X search.

2. How Does It Work?

The system uses a full-stack architecture consisting of a Python FastAPI backend and a React-based frontend.

Data Acquisition: The backend connects to NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) services through the Table Access Protocol (TAP) to retrieve available SPHEREx observational data. It processes genuine Level-2 FITS products, including science images, variance maps, quality flags, and wavelength calibration information. Astropy handles FITS operations and World Coordinate System (WCS) transformations.

Multi-Epoch Image Analysis: The platform provides image alignment, comparison, difference imaging, and inverse-variance weighted stacking. Users can explore observations from different epochs and investigate changes in celestial sources.

Astrometric Motion Detection: The motion-tracking engine measures source centroid displacement across epochs, calculates positional uncertainties, and evaluates whether observed movement is statistically significant. Gaia DR3 and Minor Planet Center (MPC) catalog information can provide external reference points for crossmatching.

Infrared Photometry and Spectroscopy: Aperture photometry extracts source fluxes and estimates signal-to-noise ratios. The spectral analysis module examines available wavelength-dependent measurements and compares spectral energy distributions against four physical templates: main-sequence stars, brown dwarfs, circumstellar disks, and icy trans-Neptunian objects.

Scientific Verification: The system evaluates six scientific hypotheses using measurable statistical criteria, uncertainty estimates, null-hypothesis testing, and synthetic source injection-recovery experiments.

3. What Makes It Creative and Different?

Our central innovation is the integration of Karl Popper's Scientific Falsification Principle into an astronomical exploration platform.

Most visualization tools focus on displaying unusual image features. However, an unusual residual does not automatically represent a real astronomical discovery.

SPHEREx TimeLens takes a different approach: every potential finding must withstand scientific testing. It distinguishes between supported hypotheses, rejected hypotheses, candidate detections, non-detections, and inconclusive results.

Its six-hypothesis verification framework evaluates observation availability, proper motion, difference imaging, infrared variability, spectral authenticity, and algorithmic detection sensitivity.

The platform also generates SHA-256-based scientific audit certificates to help preserve analysis provenance, input information, observational epochs, and verification thresholds.

4. Technologies and Tools Used

Backend and Scientific Computing:

  • Python 3.12+
  • FastAPI and Pydantic
  • NumPy and SciPy
  • Astropy for FITS, WCS, coordinates, and astronomical calculations
  • Pillow for image processing
  • Pytest for automated testing

Frontend and Visualization:

  • React 18 and TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • HTML5 Canvas and SVG for interactive astronomical visualization

Astronomical Data and External References:

  • NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA)
  • SPHEREx Level-2 FITS data
  • Gaia DR3
  • IAU Minor Planet Center (MPC)

Development and Quality Assurance:

  • Git and GitHub
  • GitHub Actions for continuous integration
  • SHA-256 for tamper-evident audit verification

5. Intended Benefits and Impact

SPHEREx TimeLens aims to bridge the gap between raw astronomical observations and scientific understanding. It provides an accessible environment for exploring infrared astronomy without requiring users to independently build complex data-processing pipelines.

Its potential applications include identifying candidate moving objects, studying variable stars, examining brown dwarf spectral characteristics, investigating infrared transients, and exploring the outer Solar System.

Most importantly, it encourages responsible scientific interpretation. By explicitly reporting uncertainty, testing alternative explanations, and allowing hypotheses to be rejected, the platform discourages false discoveries and promotes reproducible scientific investigation.

Our ultimate vision is to transform SPHEREx observations into an interactive scientific experience where anyone can explore the infrared universe while understanding not only what the data reveals, but also what it cannot yet prove.
